import turtle
import colorsys
screen = turtle.Screen().bgcolor(‘black’)
anms = turtle.Turtle()
anms.width(3)
anms.speed(0)

#Follow @apran_khunger
h = 0
n = 200
def space(x):

  anms.penup()
 anms.fd(x)
 anms.pendown()
for i in range(100):
 c = colorsys.hsv_to_rgb(h, 1, 0.8)
 h += 1/n
  anms.color(c)
 anms.forward(i*5)
 space(0)
 anms.left(145)
 for j in range (10):
 anms.fd(10)
 anms.rt(61)
turtle.mainloop()

Prompt I used : “As of now the AI is taking programmers job so what should I do to prevent mine !”

Here’s what ChatGPT said 👇 ( summarized )

It’s understandable to feel concerned about the impact of AI on job roles, including programming. However, it’s essential to remember that AI is not here to replace programmers entirely but to augment their capabilities. Here are some steps you can take to future-proof your career as a programmer:

Stay Updated: If you learn new technologies and keep updating your skills then it will make you more valuable 

Specialize: Consider specializing in a niche area of programming where human creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills are indispensable. 

Collaborate with AI: Instead of seeing AI as a threat, embrace it as a tool to enhance your work. Learn how to leverage AI technologies to improve your productivity and the quality of your code.

Diversify Your Skills: Explore interdisciplinary skills that complement programming, such as project management, user experience design, or business analysis. Having a diverse skill set can make you more adaptable to changes in the job market.

By adopting these strategies, you can position yourself to thrive in a rapidly changing technological landscape and mitigate the risk of AI replacing your job as a programmer.

Elon Musk’s Neuralink has installed a brain implant in a second patient, the Tesla CEO said in a podcast. The brain implant, as per Musk, is designed to give paralyzed patients the ability to use digital devices by thinking alone. Giving details of the second participant, Musk told podcast host Lex Fridman that the person had a spinal cord injury similar to the first patient, who was paralyzed in a diving accident.
